notes: Actual results for the fiscal year ended March 31, 2024, as the township reported them in its Annual Financial Report to the Illinois Comptroller. Not a budget.

Public schools are run by separate school districts with their own taxes, so they are not included. Residents also pay Madison County; park, library and fire protection districts are separate governments too.
Illinois townships maintain township roads, assess property and provide general assistance; most also cover the cities and villages inside them.

Covers the general, special revenue, capital projects, debt service and enterprise (utility) funds. Pension trusts and other fiduciary funds, internal service funds and component units are left out, as are transfers between funds and borrowing.
Depreciation ($12,979) is left out; capital outlay is counted when paid.
Capital outlay outside utility funds ($726,179) is reported without a function, so it is spread over the township's services in proportion to their spending.
Courts, legal services, public buildings, housing and community development count as overhead.
Debt is bonds, contracts and other long-term debt outstanding at year end (beginning balance plus new debt less debt retired), as reported.

Political money is not scored: no candidates for mayor or village president, council or board, clerk and other local offices of Wood River Township reported contributions to the State Board of Elections since 2023.
